penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Any cross-tenant M365 mailbox bridge requires tenant-level admin consent, Azure AD app registration, and per-client credential management — this is per-customer manual IT work that cannot be automated away.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling to IT admins managing corporate tenants will require sales calls or technical onboarding sessions to obtain admin consent and configure trust relationships.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Cross-tenant identity and email delegation issues are notoriously fragile; ongoing support demand would be high.

rationale: The pain is real and recurring — IT admins juggling multiple M365 tenants face this daily — but the solution is fundamentally a Microsoft-infrastructure problem requiring Azure AD/Entra app registration, cross-tenant access policies, and per-tenant admin consent flows. This is deep Microsoft-platform engineering, not a Claude-automatable service. The buyer exists (paying M365 admin), but the delivery is completely outside what this factory can build or run autonomously. Signal strength is also a single data point.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using this factory. The cross-tenant mailbox delegation gap is a structural Microsoft architecture limitation; solving it requires building an Azure AD multi-tenant application with admin consent flows, OAuth token management, and Microsoft Graph API integration — this is a full SaaS product requiring a developer team, not a prompt-plus-Stripe service. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (3, well below 6 floor) and operational_autonomy (2, well below 7 floor). Structural Microsoft architecture constraint means no clean software-layer workaround exists without deep platform engineering.
